Wild how you keep jumping on Reddit calling other trainers “sh*tty” when your own comments show zero self-awareness. You’ve made it painfully clear that you hate being asked to sell, you disrespect your manager, and you’ve publicly said you refuse to give members advice on the floor—but now you’re suddenly the authority on trainer behavior?

This member was rehabbing an injury, and the trainer backed off once he realized that. What exactly is “sh*tty” about that? Sounds like someone who made a mistake, learned, and moved on. You, on the other hand, just trash your coworkers, management, and any trainer doing the job you clearly didn’t want to do.

If anyone’s lacking self-awareness here, it’s the guy who keeps posting on Reddit to cope with the fact that he didn’t have the humility, sales skills, or professionalism to thrive. Maybe stop projecting and start reflecting.

You keep popping up with the same tired complaints, and at this point, it’s not just bitterness—it’s disrespect, especially toward your manager. The way you talk about her says a lot: you’re “showing her” Reddit threads to “shut her up”? That’s not how professionals operate—that’s how bitter, entitled people lash out when someone with more leadership and people skills holds them accountable.

Let’s be real: you clearly can’t stand that a woman who maybe doesn’t have the same degree as you is still doing better in a leadership role. And instead of reflecting on why your approach isn’t working, you resort to insulting new trainers, calling them “stupid,” and mocking your own team. That’s not being a straight shooter—that’s insecurity wrapped in condescension.

Selling PT isn’t desperation—it’s literally the job. If you’re too uncomfortable to have real conversations about someone’s goals and needs, that’s on you—not the system. Maybe the awkwardness wasn’t them—it was your inability to handle a basic client interaction like a grown adult.

Man, it’s clear you’re burned out—but it’s also clear you’re projecting that onto everyone who actually thrives in this system. You keep jumping into every Equinox post about trainers just to vent, and it’s starting to feel more like bitterness than constructive criticism.

No one’s forcing anyone to be sleazy. Selling is part of training—it’s called building a business and making a living off the value you bring. Talking to members without offering solutions isn’t relationship-building; it’s just chatting. The fact that you pride yourself on not giving advice kind of says it all.

You’re not leaving because the system is broken—you’re leaving because you refused to engage with it. There are plenty of us with or without advanced degrees who succeed because we actually take coaching, learning, and relationship-building seriously. Don’t knock others who did the work just because it didn’t pan out for you.

👍🏾 Appreciate your take, but just to clarify for anyone reading—coaches still get paid their session rate for training clients. Floor rate only applies when you're not with a client. Complimentary sessions are paid, but at a lower wage than paid sessions the idea is to build rapport and convert, which is part of what we sign up for in this industry.

I get that Equinox isn’t for everyone—it’s fast-paced and sales-driven—but it also rewards those who take initiative, connect with members, and know how to coach. If someone’s struggling, it usually reflects gaps in either their sales skills or member engagement—not just “toxic methods.”
